New York City Airbnb Market Insights

Will booking a private room always be cheaper than booking an entire home or apartment?
Source: Inside Airbnb · New York City · Dataset dated 14 September 2026 · Advertised nightly prices in USD
Executive finding: Private rooms are generally cheaper than entire homes/apartments in New York City, but they are not always cheaper. Manhattan and 17 eligible neighborhoods demonstrate exceptions. Overall medians: $115.15 for private rooms versus $218.00 for entire homes/apartments.
Room type and borough filters update the KPIs and charts. Neighborhood selection highlights a location in the ranking; it does not change the underlying comparison.

1. Price distribution by room type

Box plots show median, interquartile range and flagged/extreme observations. All valid prices are retained.
Price distributions are strongly right-skewed. The median is more representative of the typical listing than the mean.

2. Median price by borough and room type

Advertised nightly-price medians; sample size shown in each hover tooltip.
Manhattan is the borough-level exception: private-room median $256.00 versus $254.54 for entire homes/apartments.

3. Neighborhood price difference ranking

Private-room median minus entire-home median. Positive = private rooms cost more. Includes the 95 neighborhoods meeting n ≥ 10 in both categories.
Largest positive differences: Little Italy (+$355.92; n=23 vs 69) and Murray Hill (+$308.24; n=72 vs 247). Seventeen eligible neighborhoods have positive differences.

4. Missing-price percentage by borough and room type

Missing advertised-price count divided by all listings in each borough × room-type group.
Missing prices are unevenly distributed. Entire homes/apartments have 38.39% missing prices versus 32.23% for private rooms overall, which may affect representativeness.

Methodology, limitations and source

Price measure: price_numeric is the sole advertised nightly-price field used. Quote-based price fields are excluded and not combined with advertised prices.

Missing data: Missing prices are not imputed. KPIs and charts report available-price sample sizes and missingness. Filtered views recalculate statistics on the selected listing scope.

Outliers: All valid-price observations, including the 1,650 IQR-flagged high-price records, remain in the primary analysis. No values are deleted or capped.

Neighborhood eligibility: Chart 3 uses the 95 neighborhoods with at least 10 valid priced listings in each primary room type. The 128 remaining neighborhoods are excluded from that direct comparison only.

Interpretation: These are descriptive comparisons of listing-level advertised nightly prices, not actual booking transaction costs or causal effects. Listings differ in guest capacity, property characteristics, amenities, availability, fees, taxes and discounts.

Source: Inside Airbnb, New York City summary listings, 14 September 2026. Analytical basis: completed Stage 3 EDA and cleaned Stage 2 dataset.

Interactive charts use Plotly.js loaded from its public CDN. An internet connection is required when opening this HTML file.
